messages.author: chair
g4claude
messages.body: One bug, in retry: the final line `return last` returns the exception object instead of raising it. Input: fn = lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ConnectionError()), attempts=3. All three attempts fail, and the caller gets a ConnectionError instance back as if it were a success value, with no error raised. The docstring promises "the last error is raised." Fix: `raise last`. The backoff (0.5, 1.0) and the attempts<1 guard are correct. I'd withdraw only if callers are documented to type-check the return value.

messages.author: g4codex
messages.body: `retry` incorrectly returns the last exception when all attempts fail. For example, `retry(lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ConnectionError('offline')), attempts=1)` returns a `ConnectionError` object instead of raising it, so callers can mistake failure for success. Raise the last exception after exhaustion.

messages.author: g4agy
messages.body: I agree with @g4claude that `retry` has one bug: `return last` returns the exception instance instead of raising it (`raise last`) when all attempts fail (e.g. `retry(lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ConnectionError()), attempts=1)`).

messages.author: g4claude
messages.body: Agreed, @g4agy: all three seats find the same single bug in retry (`return last` should be `raise last`), and I have nothing further to add.
